design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 04C / § 05 trap mechanics: a skill roll (CARACTÉRISTIQUE + DIFFICULTÉ) with ✓ RÉUSSITE / ✕ ÉCHEC reveal texts (the only semantic colours, green/red), and the « VARIANTE PIÈGE — échec sanctionné »: ✕ échec du jet → mène directement à « Mort du personnage ». Mounted via node-editor's « Action requise » seam. Low-fi wireframe.

plan.goal: Let an author configure a node's « Piège » action — a description, the player-facing reveal text per roll outcome (réussite/échec), and whether a failed roll is lethal — mounted via the ActionRegistry, reusing the shared outcome editor.
acceptance_criteria: action-trap self-registers a « Piège » editor with the brain ActionRegistry; node-editor's « Action requise » control offers « Piège » alongside Décor/PNJ/Monstre with zero node-editor changes (Open/Closed, KR-051) — completing all four action types.
Selecting « Piège » mounts the editor for that node; structural screens (sommaire/mort) never show it.
The editor captures a trap description + a player-facing reveal text for each of the two outcomes; all persisted on the node via BookService.

The two outcomes are réussite/échec — the only semantic outcomes/colours — rendered via the SHARED brain OutcomesEditor (derived from ROLL_OUTCOMES, KR-117/091), the same rows the monster editor uses; no per-feature copy.
A « L'échec mène à la Mort » toggle captures the « échec sanctionné » variant, persisted on the node (the automatic →Mort edge is wired in a later iteration, KR-067).

All trap config is persisted through BookService.updateNode (no private copy, KR-020) and lives on the node document; action-trap and node-editor never import each other (wired at the composition root).
The editor renders strictly from design-system primitives/tokens (Field, OutcomesEditor, Toggle), light theme; controls are keyboard-operable with ≥44px targets.
plan.walking_skeleton: registerActionTrap registers an ActionEditor { type:'piege', label:'Piège', render } with the brain ActionRegistry (wired at the App composition root). TrapEditor reads node.trap live via useOpenBook and writes via BookService.updateNode: a DESCRIPTION Field, the shared brain OutcomesEditor for the réussite/échec reveal texts, and a « L'échec mène à la Mort » Toggle (fatal). Skill caractéristique/difficulté + the automatic →Mort edge are later iterations.

iterations.goal: Skill roll (§ 05): CARACTÉRISTIQUE select + DIFFICULTÉ; the roll gates which outcome applies; surface réussite/échec.
Wire outcome targets through edges; the « échec sanctionné » fatal flag creates/maintains the automatic →Mort link (KR-067), not the manual edge API.
Trap-on-object variant (a décor « prendre » object that triggers a trap roll) — share the roll model with action-decor.

known_risks: KR-050/051 — node-editor is a host: action-trap self-registers via the ActionRegistry and is mounted without being imported; adding the action needs zero node-editor changes.

KR-092 — a trap is a réussite/échec skill roll; its outcome rows reuse the SHARED brain OutcomesEditor (KR-109) derived from ROLL_OUTCOMES (KR-117/091) — never a per-feature copy of the rows or the labels. The « échec → Mort » fatal flag captures intent now; the actual automatic →Mort edge is wired later via the dedicated combat/trap path, not the manual edge API (KR-067).
KR-020 — trap config is read/written through BookService (the SSOT); the editor holds no private copy and reflects live via useOpenBook.
KR-090 — trap config lives on the node document (node.trap); structural screens never carry it (updateNode's text-only guard for sommaire/mort, KR-055).
KR-013 — derive the editor's current values inline from the live node, not via a useEffect-synced mirror.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: Fourth and final action-* feature: self-registers with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionTrap) — node-editor now offers all four action types (Décor/PNJ/Monstre/Piège) with zero changes (KR-050/051).

Extracted a shared brain OutcomesEditor (KR-109) at the SECOND consumer of the réussite/échec rows: monster + trap now render outcomes from one component (derived from ROLL_OUTCOMES, KR-117/091); MonsterEditor was refactored to use it, removing the duplicated rows. Same lesson as ObjectEditor.
TrapEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020), normalised once (DEFAULT_TRAP); trap config lives on node.trap, NodePatch carries it (text-only guard keeps it off structural screens, KR-055/090).
The « échec sanctionné » variant is a fatal boolean on the trap; the automatic →Mort edge it implies is deferred (KR-067), so the skeleton captures intent without manual edges into Mort.
deviations_from_plan: Skill caractéristique/difficulté, outcome-target wiring, the automatic →Mort edge, and the trap-on-object variant are deferred to iterations 1–3; the skeleton ships description + réussite/échec texts + the fatal flag.

test_coverage.integration: action-trap via App — « Piège » offered through the registry seam; description, both réussite/échec texts (shared OutcomesEditor), and the fatal toggle persisted; structural-screen guard now covers trap (BookService)

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: The skill roll (§ 05): TrapConfig gained a roll (SkillRoll) — a CARACTÉRISTIQUE SegmentedControl + a DIFFICULTÉ Stepper (the shared brain primitive). The réussite/échec reveal texts stay in trap.outcomes (shared OutcomesEditor), so the roll only carries trait + difficulty — SkillRoll.failureText was made OPTIONAL so trap and décor share one roll shape (décor sets failureText, trap does not).

Caractéristiques became a brain CHARACTERISTICS registry (Characteristic union + Record{label}, KR-117) — placed in brain like ROLL_OUTCOMES because skill-roll editors reuse it (trap now; décor « jet requis » later). The select options + labels derive from it, never a hardcoded list or a trait === branch. Fulfils the décor-iter-1 note that the caractéristique catalog would be extracted at the second consumer.

A skeleton trap (description + outcomes + fatal, no roll) migrates the default roll in on read ({ ...DEFAULT_TRAP, ...node.trap }, KR-116) and canonicalises on write. TrapEditor stays a VIEW over BookService (KR-020); the « échec sanctionné » fatal flag still captures intent, its automatic →Mort edge deferred to iteration 2 (KR-067).
deviations_from_plan: action-decor's « jet requis » still uses a free-text caractéristique Field + a numeric Field (its shipped iter-1 UX); adopting the shared CHARACTERISTICS select + Stepper there is a décor product change left for a later décor iteration — not bundled into this trap slice (the registry is in brain, ready). Difficulté bounds are a low-fi 1–12 target number.

« the roll gates which outcome applies » is captured in authoring (the roll config sits beside the réussite/échec texts); the actual play-time gating + the automatic échec→Mort edge are iteration 2 (KR-067).

test_coverage.unit: (shared) CHARACTERISTICS exercised via the trap caractéristique radios
test_coverage.integration: action-trap via App — caractéristique select (Endurance) + difficulté stepper persist on trap.roll; a pre-roll trap migrates the default roll in without clobbering description/outcomes/fatal (KR-116); existing description/outcomes/fatal test still green
test_coverage.review_note: Pre-commit tech-lead review (APPROVE): folded in the migration test, hoisted the roll-section inline style to a const, and commented the intentional roll.trait cast.

open_questions: Skill roll model (caractéristique/difficulté) — shared with the décor « jet requis » (iteration 1/3).
The automatic échec→Mort edge (KR-067) and outcome targets (iteration 2).
